title: Earl Bostic's style and a ailing friend's 15 minutes a day
summary: Dejan says Bostic's recorded style was that of Theodore Purnell, a close friend now recovering who can play 15 minutes a day; the interviewers consider recording him.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Another thing you were telling us was that Earl Bostic, you say, got a lot of his stuff from you now.

Well, Earl Bostic was very fast on the saxophone. Very fast. Very good musician and everything. But the style he played on the record, that's the style that Thereto Poino used to play around here. Yeah. That's the style. Every time I heard Earl Bostic's record, I said that. That's right. Have you seen Pernell lately or? I saw him at the banquet we had. Oh, yeah.
Somebody else thought maybe told me that he's recovering a little bit now.

Well, I don't know. He and I had a personal friend of mine. We'd come up together, very personal friend of mine. I'd sit in his car and talk to him at least 45 minutes after we left the banquet. And he's talking to the doctor, so he'd play 15 minutes a day. He plays clarinet, very good clarinet player. And he bought his saxophone at night and he played about 15 minutes, that was it. But he still got something. He still played.
How's his memory? Is his memory all right?

Pretty good, because you could tell by the head numbers he played, because when he picked up his horn, I would stand right there by him, because I always used to tell him, like him or St. George, I said, I see him at the horn, let me play. You know? I mean, kid wasn't that like that. He might tell me why I'm playing. He said, give me this horn. But I went stand by him, and listened at him, and he was just playing a couple of head numbers, and he was right in there.
Right in there. And people sang it, sometimes he'd just say, couldn't remember how a certain little simple tune went.

Well, he say, you say that did him good, that Sunday. He said, I didn't think I could play in time even. He said, how did? I said, you sound like you're never just stop playing for us, I'm concerned. It really was good. Yeah, sure, very good. We ought to go down to his house one time.
We want to interview him, but I was wondering about, also, you know, we don't like to bother somebody if they're not feeling it.
We go down and talk, and we ask him how long he could sit down and talk, and then when he say how long he could talk, well, then he'd blow.
Even if it's only 15 minutes a day.
The doctor told me he could blow 15 minutes a day.
He could talk in 15 minutes all right, too.
